methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting community access in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capability-building outside traditional tech hubs, directly countering concentration by creating peer-learning networks that could enable distributed deep literacy.

signals.title: Virginia Tech Researchers Use AI to Gauge Manufacturing Water Needs - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech researchers developing specialized AI for manufacturing water needs demonstrates deep technical capability concentrated in academic research centers, but unclear pathways for distributing this expertise to manufacturers across rural regions who would benefit.

signals.title: Meta, Google invest in skilled worker training to build Virginia data centers - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Meta and Google funding worker training for data center operations suggests platform companies are creating shallow, operationally-focused AI adoption rather than deep capability development—workers learn to maintain infrastructure, not build or customize AI systems.

signals.title: How AI is changing what happens to Hampton Roads' trash - The Suffolk News-Herald
signals.signal_reading: AI deployed in municipal waste management represents turnkey platform adoption that spreads geographically but remains shallow—cities consume vendor solutions without developing internal AI development capacity or transferable skills.

signals.title: Virginia Tech's AI Model Aims to Ease Drought Water Conflicts - AGDAILY
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's AI drought model addresses critical agricultural needs across the state, but the capability remains concentrated in Blacksburg researchers rather than distributed to farmers or regional extension networks who could adapt and apply the technology locally.
